title: Signs of dehydration
asks: how do I know if I am dehydrated
dark urine and tired am I dehydrated
dizzy when I stand up and very thirsty
havent peed all day is that bad
how bad is dehydration when to worry
answer: Common signs of dehydration: dark urine with a strong odor; low urine output; dry mouth, tongue, throat and lips; dark, sunken eyes; fatigue or lethargy; headache; lack of appetite; stomach cramps or vomiting; emotional instability; a trench line down the center of the tongue; thirst.
Skin pinch: if you pinch the skin, the fold returns slowly to its former position. Capillary refill under the fingernails is delayed (normal is less than 3 seconds).
Thirst is not an adequate indicator of the need to drink: by the time you feel thirsty, you are already dehydrated.
Urine: small amounts of darker urine may indicate substantial dehydration. Dark yellow or brown urine indicates dehydration.
As it gets worse: heart rate and breathing rate increase; urine output, mental status and muscular strength decrease; the person often feels weak or dizzy when upright.

In children: very dry mouth and lips; lethargy (excessive drowsiness, slow to respond, not interactive); sunken eyes; small amounts of dark urine; in infants under 1 year, a sunken soft spot (fontanelle); abnormal skin pinch.
If water is plentiful, drink enough to ensure a steady urine output throughout the day.
warnings: Red skin indicates a severe condition needing immediate medical evacuation.
Untreated dehydration can lead to altered mental status, headaches, weakness, cramping, fainting, convulsions, shock, coma and even death.
Get medical advice early for a markedly dehydrated person, and whenever there is any question about hydration or mental state. Lost fluid can be replaced by mouth or into a vein (intravenous).
Children become dehydrated more rapidly than adults. Infants and young children are particularly at risk because they cannot say when they are thirsty and cannot drink more on their own.
Over-hydration can cause low sodium levels in the blood that can lead to death.

quotes.text: Common signs and symptoms of dehydration include— z Dark urine with strong odor. z Low urine output. z Dark, sunken eyes. z Fatigue. z Emotional instability. z Skin inelasticity. z Capillary refill delayed under fingernails. z Trench line down center of tongue. z Thirst. Thirst is not an adequate indicator of the need to drink water. Once personnel are thirsty, they are already dehydrated.

Common symptoms of dehydration are— • Red skin indicating a severe condition needing immediate medical evacuation to the nearest medical treatment facility. • Lack of appetite. • The mouth, tongue, and throat are dry. • Stomach cramps and/or vomiting. • Headaches.
By the time a Soldier feels thirsty, they are already dehydrated and should drink water whenever possible, particularly during halts.
Check urine in the snow for dark yellow or brown spots that indicate dehydration.
Signs of dehydration - Is the mouth very dry? Do the eyeballs seem unusually sunken? If you pinch the skin, does the fold return slowly to its former position?
Check fluid status: In dehydration states, the patient may feel thirsty or may have dry lips and mouth, abnormal skin pinch, lethargy, and delayed capillary refill.
Check urine: Check the urine colour and volume. Small amounts of darker urine may indicate substantial dehydration.

In the adult, assessment of hydration status is often based on observation of clinical signs and symptoms. The heart rate and respiratory rate both increase. Urine output, skin turgor, mental status and muscular strength decrease. The patient frequently complains of feeling weak or dizzy when in the upright position.

If left untreated, dehydration results in a downward spiral that further depletes essential fluids and electrolytes (primarily water, potassium, sodium chloride and bicarbonate and resulting changes in acid-base balance). These fluids and electrolyte shifts can lead to altered mental status, headaches, weakness, cramping, fainting, convulsions, shock, coma and even death.
Once a patient has become dehydrated the two available routes of fluid replacement are oral and intravenous.
Early communication with medical specialists ashore is critical in taking care of a markedly dehydrated patient at sea.
Advice should also be sought if there is any question regarding hydration status, mentation, or lack of response to therapy.

Signs of dehydration in children • Very dry mouth and lips • Lethargy (excessive drowsiness and slowness to respond), child not interactive • Sunken eyes • Small amounts of dark urine (ask about number of nappies for infants) • Sunken fontanelles in infants under 1 year • Delayed capillary refill (normal capillary refill is less than 3 seconds) • Abnormal skin pinch

Children have a relatively larger surface area (compared to their body volume) and are thus likely to become dehydrated more rapidly. Infants and young children are particularly at risk as they are unable to say when they are thirsty and cannot drink more on their own.
If water is plentiful, drink enough water to ensure a steady urine output throughout the day. However, over-hydration can cause low serum sodium levels that can lead to death.

conflict: THIRST AS A GUIDE: ATP 3-50.21 (2018), TC 21-3 (2025) and TB MED 507 (2022) say thirst is not adequate and by the time you are thirsty you are already dehydrated; JTS Altitude Emergencies 2024 says hydration at altitude should be 'guided by thirst and appropriate urine output'. 'RED SKIN' as the sign of a severe condition comes only from TC 21-3 (cold-weather manual); no other kit source lists it. TREATMENT is not on this card: TC 21-3 says keep the victim warm, give plenty of liquids and rest; HHS Ship's Medicine Chest 2003 gives oral rehydration solution and IV fluids; see the oral-rehydration-solution card. FEMA P-2064 (2020) has nothing on dehydration signs.
